# Baruch Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And the Lord our God has made good his word which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged Israel, and against our kings and our rulers and the men of Israel and Judah —

**2** to bring upon us great evils which have not been done under the whole heaven, such as were done in Jerusalem, according to what is written in the law of Moses —

**3** that one man should eat the flesh of his son and the flesh of his daughter.

**4** And he gave them to be subject to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the peoples round about, where the Lord has scattered them.

**5** And they were cast down and not raised up, because we sinned against the Lord our God, in not listening to his voice.

**6** To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers belongs shame of face, as it is this day.

**7** All these evils have come upon us which the Lord threatened against us.

**8** And we did not entreat the favor of the Lord, to turn each of us from the thoughts of his evil heart.

**9** And the Lord kept watch over the evils and brought them upon us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he has commanded us;

**10** yet we have not obeyed his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord which he set before us.

**11** And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and signs and wonders and with great power and with an outstretched arm, and made yourself a name, as it is to this day —

**12** we have sinned, we have acted impiously, we have acted unjustly, O Lord our God, against all your ordinances.

**13** Let your wrath turn away from us, for we are left as a few among the nations where you have scattered us.

**14** Hear, O Lord, our prayer and our supplication, and deliver us for your own sake, and grant us favor in the sight of those who have carried us into exile,

**15** that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, for Israel and his descendants have been called by your name.

**16** Look down, O Lord, from your holy dwelling and consider us; incline your ear, O Lord, and hear us;

**17** open your eyes and see — for it is not the dead in Hades who will give glory and justification to the Lord,

**18** but the soul that is grieved over the greatness of evil, who walks bowed and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul — these give glory and righteousness to you, O Lord.

**19** For not upon the righteousness of our fathers do we lay before you our supplication, O Lord our God,

**20** but because you have sent your wrath and your anger upon us, as you have spoken through your servants the prophets, saying:

**21** "Thus says the Lord: Bow your shoulder and serve the king of Babylon, and remain in the land which I gave to your fathers.

**22** But if you will not hear the voice of the Lord and serve the king of Babylon,

**23** I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah and from outside Jerusalem the voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and all the land will become a desolation, without inhabitant."

**24** And we did not listen to your voice, to serve the king of Babylon; and you made good your words which you spoke through your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be brought out from their places,

**25** and indeed they were thrown out to the heat of day and the frost of night, and they died in great misery, by famine and sword and by exile.

**26** And you made the house over which your name was called as it is this day, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

**27** Yet you dealt with us, O Lord our God, according to all your kindness and according to all your great compassion,

**28** as you spoke through your servant Moses, on the day when you commanded him to write your law before the children of Israel, saying:

**29** "If you will not hear my voice, this great noisy crowd will certainly become small among the nations where I will scatter them.

**30** For I know that they will not hear me, for they are a stiff-necked people; but they will turn to their heart in the land of their exile,

**31** and they will know that I am the Lord their God. And I will give them a heart and ears that hear,

**32** and they will praise me in the land of their exile, and will remember my name,

**33** and they will turn from their stubbornness and from their wicked deeds, for they will remember the way of their fathers who sinned before the Lord.

**34** And I will bring them back again to the land which I swore to give to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and they will rule over it; and I will multiply them, and they will not be diminished.

**35** And I will make with them an everlasting covenant, to be their God and they shall be my people; and I will no more remove my people Israel from the land which I have given them."

---
*EMET notes: v.3 cannibalism quotation follows Deut 28:53-57, Lam 4:10 — a horrifying fulfillment motif. v.11 "mighty hand" Exodus formula retained. vv.21-23 prophetic oracle closely parallels Jer 27:12-13. v.34 "Abraham and Isaac and Jacob" preserves the patriarchal formula.*
